binders: An arbitrary scalar field q : Real -> Real -> Real and arbitrary real speed, x, and t.
conclusions: The pointwise Fin 1 vector conservation residual for the one-component embedding of q with coefficient matrix [speed] holds if and only if the pointwise scalar transport residual for q with the same speed holds.
mathematical_definitions: The embedded vector field is Q(x,t)(0)=q(x,t).
The coefficient matrix is the 1 by 1 matrix [speed].
The vector predicate requires derivative vectors Q_t,Q_x and Q_t+[speed]Q_x=0; the scalar predicate requires real derivatives q_t,q_x and q_t+speed*q_x=0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every scalar space-time field q, real speed, and point (x,t), viewing q as a one-component vector and the speed as a 1 by 1 coefficient matrix makes the vector conservation-law residual exactly equivalent to the scalar advection residual. Both sides are pointwise existential differentiability statements: suitable time and space derivatives must exist and satisfy the corresponding zero-residual equation.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The equivalence is only for one real component (Fin 1) and a constant scalar coefficient matrix.
It is pointwise and does not assert that q is differentiable or solves either PDE; if the required derivatives do not exist, both predicates may simply be false.
No sign, nonzero, or regularity assumption is imposed on speed, and no initial data, boundary data, uniqueness, or global solution statement is encoded.
